facts.text: ISO 3450 defines stopping distance from brake-control actuation to standstill, including brake-system reaction but excluding operator reaction.
facts.quote: ISO 3450's stopping distance runs from brake-control actuation to standstill and so includes brake-system reaction while excluding operator reaction.

facts.text: ISO 21815 adds upstream time for object detection, confirmation and determination, collision-risk computation, and intervention initiation; these processes consume distance before deceleration builds.
facts.quote: ISO 21815 adds upstream time: object detection, confirmation and determination, collision-risk computation and intervention initiation all consume distance before deceleration builds.

facts.text: The published brake-delay figures in this passage are architecture-specific.
A peer-reviewed Materials publication from 2026 reports pressure response under 0.3 s for a tracked-vehicle electro-hydraulic brake.
facts.quote: Tracked-vehicle electro-hydraulic brake | Pressure response under 0.3 s | Peer-reviewed, Materials, 2026 [6]

facts.text: A 2025 conference chapter reports that a mining electric vehicle electro-hydraulic brake-by-wire system reached its design value in 0.41 s.
facts.quote: Mining electric vehicle electro-hydraulic brake-by-wire | Design value reached in 0.41 s; 0.09 s faster with regenerative assist | Conference chapter, 2025 [7]

facts.text: A 2025 conference chapter reports that regenerative assist made a mining electric vehicle electro-hydraulic brake-by-wire system reach its design value 0.09 s faster.
facts.quote: Mining electric vehicle electro-hydraulic brake-by-wire | Design value reached in 0.41 s; 0.09 s faster with regenerative assist | Conference chapter, 2025 [7]

facts.text: TRB Record 1208 (1989) reports about 0.5 s inherent delay for road truck air brakes; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Road truck air brakes | About 0.5 s inherent delay | TRB Record 1208, 1989 **(on-road evidence)** [8]

facts.text: US MSHA Table M-1 assumes 0.5 s to 2.5 s system response by weight class, plus 1 s operator time.
facts.quote: US MSHA Table M-1 regulatory assumption | 0.5 s to 2.5 s system response by weight class, plus 1 s operator time | Regulation text [2]

facts.text: A historic US mining government report gives about 2 s nominal operator reaction for large haulage trucks.
facts.quote: Large haulage trucks, historic US mining study | About 2 s nominal operator reaction plus 1 s to 2 s additional lag for dynamic retarders; friction brakes behaved differently at low speed | Government report, historic [9]

facts.text: A historic US mining government report gives 1 s to 2 s additional lag for dynamic retarders on large haulage trucks.
facts.quote: Large haulage trucks, historic US mining study | About 2 s nominal operator reaction plus 1 s to 2 s additional lag for dynamic retarders; friction brakes behaved differently at low speed | Government report, historic [9]

facts.text: A historic US mining government report found that friction brakes on large haulage trucks behaved differently from dynamic retarders at low speed.
facts.quote: Large haulage trucks, historic US mining study | About 2 s nominal operator reaction plus 1 s to 2 s additional lag for dynamic retarders; friction brakes behaved differently at low speed | Government report, historic [9]

facts.text: The historic retarder figures show that delay can dominate stopping distance.
facts.quote: The historic retarder figures show that delay can dominate stopping distance

facts.text: The historic retarder delay figures are not valid design constants for a 2027 system.
facts.quote: they are not valid design constants for a 2027 system.

facts.text: South African guidance MHSC SIM 040502 for brake testing of trackless mining machinery measures response time from brake application to 10% g of retardation; the guidance date is not stated.
facts.quote: South African guidance for brake testing of trackless mining machinery measures response time from brake application to 10% g of retardation (MHSC SIM 040502; date not stated).

facts.text: Measured response times for large wheel loaders, articulated dump trucks or haul trucks were not found in a peer-reviewed source.
